# Tagcast 1.8.0

Tagcast 1.8.0 makes the workspace more compact, brings the important settings into
a guided first setup, and adds explicit MusicBrainz track-list comparison with
reviewed title and artist correction drafts. The desktop app and browser interface
continue to share the same player, editor and data-integrity safeguards.

## A more compact workspace

- Amber Midnight adds a near-black appearance with warm gold accents. Appearance
  remains independent of Light, Dark and Auto; changing it does not restart audio.
- The left navigation starts open and can be collapsed manually. Its button stays
  reachable, and opening the right panel does not hide navigation automatically.
  Settings still controls optional shortcuts and their order.
- One right-hand panel switches between Playlist and Details. Playlist shows the
  existing local play queue; Devices is now beside its queue heading, including
  when empty, and remains available on the full Now playing page.
- Details follows the currently queued track and its original album, even while
  browsing another artist or album. Restored queues retain bounded metadata without
  loading every album. Known credits, genres, tags, numbers, ratings, upload dates
  and available technical metadata appear in read-only accordions. Unknown values
  are not invented, and a partial queue does not establish full-album totals.
- Fixed sorting buttons sit below search in the sticky album/artist toolbar.
  Clicking an active direction reverses it; Random reshuffles the complete shelf
  and has a trailing shuffle indicator. Filters remain separate. The redundant
  Play random album shortcut is removed from the album browser; Random does not
  start playback. Discovery-group random playback is unchanged.
- Header controls, breadcrumbs, filter menus and panel tabs use less space.
  Album actions now offer Play and an accessible Shuffle icon; Add to playlist
  moves into More album actions. Existing queue and editing actions remain.
- The visible shutdown finishing window follows the selected theme while keeping
  semantic warning and error colours. Accepted saves and read-backs still finish
  before shutdown; no blanket forced-termination deadline is introduced.

## First setup

- A genuinely new installation offers a short guided setup after startup settles.
  Existing installations can open it from Settings → Interface → First setup.
- Connect through the existing iBroadcast sign-in, then review playback quality,
  optional experimental gapless, lyrics source order and consent, language,
  appearance, browsing and optional services. Free-account restrictions remain.
- Steps save only on explicit confirmation and reuse normal preferences. Back,
  skipping or opening the wizard does not enable services. Failed persistence and
  account/capability changes preserve inputs and block stale submissions.
- Existing profiles are not treated as new merely after updating or disconnecting.
  No separate login, library scan or metadata write is added.

## Compare an album's track list

- Choose Compare track list… from an album's More menu. Opening shows the loaded
  album/disc set without contacting a provider. Search MusicBrainz explicitly by
  artist/title, then choose a specific edition using its date, country, medium,
  label and disc/track counts.
- Compare the complete displayed positions side by side, retaining disc numbers,
  repeated positions, version text and unknown values. Differences include titles,
  numbering and known duration differences greater than two seconds. This is a
  positional comparison, not an audio match or a claim that one edition is correct.
- Editions are paginated and bounded. Incomplete or oversized references are
  reported rather than silently compared in part. Refine the search for a different
  edition or to inspect an album containing material from multiple releases.
- Public searches send only entered artist/title text or the chosen public release
  ID to MusicBrainz, without iBroadcast credentials, audio or native track IDs.
  Source preferences, pacing and account/session/library ownership checks remain.
  Public-service errors remain visible and require a new explicit read.

## Prepare selected title and artist corrections

- Explicitly choose individual titles or artist credits to take into the ordinary
  metadata editor. Nothing is preselected, and reference rows can be chosen
  manually: Tagcast does not automatically pair, reorder, move or split tracks.
- Only selected, changed fields enter the draft. Guest artists remain separate
  credits; existing native IDs, unrelated roles and phrases are preserved. A
  release's album artist is never substituted for missing track artist credits.
- Inspect and adjust the resulting draft, then use the existing before/after
  review and Save. Comparison itself never writes. Normal fresh-state checks,
  account/session guards, serialization and read-back still apply; ambiguous
  mutations are never retried automatically.
- The editor handoff keeps focus and the Review button stable. Deferred lyrics
  responses cannot move the form during that handoff; explicit normal track or
  lyrics selection retains its existing behaviour.

## Compatibility, downloads and upgrading

- Downloads cover macOS Apple Silicon and Intel, Windows x64, Linux x64 and a
  Debian/Ubuntu package. Every package has a SHA-256 companion.
- Production macOS downloads require Developer ID signing, Apple notarization,
  stapled-ticket validation and Gatekeeper verification after extraction on both
  architectures. Publication is gated on native smoke tests, Debian installation
  checks and complete distribution verification.
- The runtime remains Electron 44.11.0. Python source use requires 3.11 or newer;
  desktop downloads include Python. Replace the complete application/package while
  retaining the normal settings folder. There is no automatic installer/updater.
- All six interface languages include the new controls, setup and comparison flow.
  Local Help and the repository guides describe their safeguards. The illustrated
  1.7.0 PDF and dated screenshots remain labelled with the version they depict;
  they have not been relabelled as a new 1.8.0 manual.

## Preserved safeguards and known limitations

Tagcast does not retag existing local music files. Explicit downloads create
separate copies; uploads and iBroadcast changes remain explicit and reviewed.
This release does not change the iBroadcast write protocol or playlist append
semantics. There are no real-account write tests as part of release validation.

- Exact iBroadcast append behaviour when a playlist already contains duplicate
  positions remains unverified (F2-02). The existing implementation is preserved;
  no mock-based assumption is presented as a verified service guarantee.
- Windows code signing remains deferred. Physical Linux Wayland testing and
  exhaustive hardware-specific audio testing remain incomplete.
- Experimental gapless remains optional and off by default; unsupported
  transitions use ordinary playback. Universal sample accuracy is not claimed.
- MusicBrainz availability and edition completeness are external limitations.
  Comparison cannot establish audio identity or resolve an ambiguous edition.
- Native focus behaviour can be affected by competing desktop automation. This
  does not replace testing on a user's actual device or audio output.

See the [Wiki](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki),
[workspace controls](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/main/docs/workspace-controls.md),
[first setup](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/main/docs/first-setup.md)
and [track-list comparison](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/main/docs/tracklist-comparison.md).
